idiom_name: hand-written adapter struct of function pointers over POSIX message queues (mq_open/mq_send/mq_receive) or libmosquitto
implementation_notes: C has no classes or interfaces, so the adapter is a struct holding the channel handle plus the application callbacks (function pointers) it must invoke, with explicit serialization into fixed-size buffers: the classic structure is hand-written, not replaced. The channel primitive can be a POSIX message queue (mq_open/mq_send/mq_receive with priorities and the O_NONBLOCK/EAGAIN contract) or a broker client such as libmosquitto, where mosquitto_publish and mosquitto_message_callback_set cover the two directions. The adapter remains the only place that knows the wire format and the queue/topic names.
pitfalls: mq_send blocks when the queue is full unless the descriptor was opened with O_NONBLOCK (which instead fails with EAGAIN); a blocking publish inside an event loop stalls the whole process.
Beyond a byte buffer there is no framing: the adapter must define and version its own wire format and validate lengths against mq_msgsize.
Callbacks registered with mosquitto_message_callback_set run on the library's network-loop thread, so shared application state needs synchronization.
